dishes.make_ahead: Make the sauce up to 3 days ahead; bake the pie up to 8 hours ahead, it is served at room temperature anyway

ingredients.item: caster sugar, 1 for the dough, 1 for the sauce
olive oil, 2 for the dough, 2 for the sauce

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, a teaspoon of sugar, the water and 2 tbsp oil into a soft dough and knead for 5 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise until doubled. Meanwhile simmer the tomatoes with 2 tbsp oil, the garlic, a teaspoon of oregano and the last of the sugar until thick.
Oil a deep baking tray, press the dough out to the edges and leave to puff. Heat the oven to 220C.
Spread the sauce thickly over the dough right to the edges and bake until the base is crisp underneath.
Cool to room temperature.
Dust with the pecorino and the rest of the oregano and cut into squares.

dishes.make_ahead: Roast and slice the pork up to 2 days ahead and keep it in its juices in the fridge; reheat gently and cook the broccolini on the night

ingredients.item: garlic cloves, crushed, 4 for the pork, 2 for the greens

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160C. Rub the pork all over with 4 of the garlic cloves, the fennel seeds, rosemary, 1 tbsp oil and plenty of salt and pepper.
Sit in a small roasting dish, pour in the stock, cover tightly with foil and roast until very tender.
Rest, then slice as thinly as you can and return the slices to the juices.
Fry the broccolini in the rest of the oil with the last 2 garlic cloves and the chilli flakes until tender and catching. Season.
Split the rolls, pile in the pork, a slice of provolone and the broccolini, and spoon over some juices.

veg.make_ahead: Roast the mushrooms up to 1 day ahead and keep them in their juices in the fridge; reheat and cook the broccolini on the night

ingredients.item: garlic cloves, crushed, 4 for the mushrooms, 2 for the greens

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the mushrooms with 4 of the garlic cloves, the fennel seeds, rosemary, 2 tbsp oil and salt and pepper.
Roast in a dish until browned, then pour in the stock and soy sauce and roast 10 minutes more.
Fry the broccolini in the rest of the oil with the last 2 garlic cloves and the chilli flakes until tender and catching. Season.
Split the rolls, pile in the mushrooms, a slice of provolone and the broccolini, and spoon over some juices.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the mash up to 1 day ahead and reheat with a splash of milk; crumb the steaks up to 4 hours ahead and keep chilled; fry and make the gravy on the night

ingredients.item: butter, 40g for the mash, 30g for the gravy
full cream milk, 80ml for the mash, 125ml for the coating, 500ml for the gravy
plain flour, 150g for the coating, 40g for the gravy

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Season the coating flour with the paprika, garlic powder and salt. Beat the eggs with the coating milk.
Pound the steaks thin between sheets of baking paper. Dip each in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing it on.
Heat the oil in a large heavy frying pan and fry the steaks for 3 to 4 minutes a side, in batches, until deep golden. Keep warm.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil. Add the gravy butter and flour, cook for 1 minute, whisk in the gravy milk and pepper and simmer until thick. Season.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the mash butter and milk. Steam the beans until tender.
Plate the steaks with the mash and beans and pour over the gravy.

veg.make_ahead: Make the mash up to 1 day ahead and reheat with a splash of milk; steam and crumb the cauliflower up to 4 hours ahead and keep chilled; fry and make the gravy on the night

ingredients.item: butter, 40g for the mash, 30g for the gravy
full cream milk, 80ml for the mash, 125ml for the coating, 500ml for the gravy
cauliflowers, each cut into 2 thick slabs through the core
plain flour, 150g for the coating, 40g for the gravy

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Steam the cauliflower slabs over the pot for 6 minutes until just tender, then pat dry.
Season the coating flour with the paprika, garlic powder and salt. Beat the eggs with the coating milk.
Dip each cauliflower slab in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing it on.
Heat the oil in a large heavy frying pan and fry the cauliflower for 3 to 4 minutes a side, in batches, until deep golden. Keep warm.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil. Add the gravy butter and flour, cook for 1 minute, whisk in the gravy milk and pepper and simmer until thick. Season.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the mash butter and milk. Steam the beans until tender.
Plate the cauliflower with the mash and beans and pour over the gravy.

dishes.make_ahead: Fry the dough balls up to 2 days ahead and keep airtight; toss in the warm honey on the day

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar, eggs, butter and both zests into a soft dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest.
Roll the dough into ropes about 1cm thick and cut into 1cm pieces.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry the pieces in batches for about 2 minutes until golden. Drain.
Warm the honey in a wide pan until runny.
Tip in the fried balls and toss to coat, then pile into a wreath on a plate and scatter with the hundreds and thousands.
Leave to set.

dishes.make_ahead: Chill the beer overnight and the glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes before pouring

steps.text: Chill 4 beer glasses and 4 shot glasses in the freezer.
Pour the whiskey into the shot glasses.
Pour the lager into the beer glasses and serve each with a shot alongside.

af.make_ahead: Brew and chill the smoky tea shot up to 3 days ahead; chill the glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes before pouring

steps.text: Brew the tea bags in the boiling water for 5 minutes, lift out and stir in the brown sugar and vanilla.
Chill the tea, and chill 4 beer glasses and 4 shot glasses in the freezer.
Pour the tea into the shot glasses.
Pour the lager into the beer glasses and serve each with a shot alongside.
